summary: Two things recorded. First, the corrected partial-restart repeat (receipt 2963a0b01d97404dbf946e7b87a214f8) reproduced the live-quorum progress loss exactly — two restarted voters with empty configurations, the untouched voter leading at index 2 with nodes_with_full=1, then no leader among the two live voters each holding log index 13, while the control re-elects at index 0 — so that claim is also reproducible and the interpretation cites it. Second, I extended the dual-majority scenario to the client-contract mechanism: while the stale-membership leader still leads with the promoted voter's acknowledgements, VerifyLeader returns success, and in the same run the old majority elects B in term 4 while A is still leader in term 3, so the documented protection against returning stale data from a peer that lost leadership does not hold in this state; the local run reproduced exactly that (verify_ok true plus a higher-term leader, verify_confirmed_while_other_leader true). The revision is submitted against the current successor of that harness (previous_id f79f8f8c97204c7d9c76b1a2b8ca07a0-experiment, after the validator correctly rejected my first attempt naming a retired predecessor) with the earlier comparisons preserved and one added for the new event.
